<div class="archive-text">State Plan for the American Rescue Plan Elementary and
Secondary School Emergency Relief Fund
• Describing the State’s Current Status and Needs (p. 4)
• #3: “Identifying Needs of Underserved Students: Describe your State’s
 2-3 highest priority academic, social, emotional, and/or mental
 health needs for the remainder of the 2020-2021 school year (if
 applicable) and for the 2021-2022 school year related to the impact
 of the COVID-19 pandemic on each of the following student groups:”
• “To the extent possible, this description should include data on
 indicators such as estimates of the academic impact of lost
 instructional time (i.e., “learning loss”) chronic absenteeism, student
 engagement, and social-emotional well-being.”
 Understanding Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Understanding pandemic related academic impact
• With the data Hawaii has from its state assessments, they are well
 positioned to investigate and address the academic impact of COVID-19.
• We are currently working with several states (including Hawaii, AZ, MA,
 RI, GA, CO) to support inferences from state assessments about the
 academic impact of the pandemic on students.
• Indiana, for example, passed legislation was passed requiring the DOE
 to produce annual reports that include analyses regarding pandemic
 related academic impact and recovery.
• Their ESSER state plan response details the learning loss report as
 evidence of compliance.
• A focal point of Center work over the last 6 months is to support such
 inferences.
 Understanding Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Understanding pandemic related academic impact
• Hawaii is well positioned with it current assessments (SBAC and ACCESS) to
 derive academic impact data from those assessments.
• See the attached learning loss paper for more details.
• For example, Indiana will use its state summative test (ILEARN) and WIDA-
 ACCESS results to determine academic impact.
• The question is not so much how or if but whether Hawaii wants to pursue
 that direction.
• Potential Problems:
 • Low participation rates (&lt; 50%) might cause issues with infernces.
 • Leadership not wanting to report/emphasize academic impact
 • Public reporting of data won’t align with academic impact use.
 Understanding Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```
